title: Adapt by declared cuts, keep hard facts
statement: When adapting a text for young readers, leave unsuitable material out by declared selection, never silent rewriting, and keep hard facts such as coercion or racism visible without endorsing them.
detail: The rebuilt drama unit retold its play for Grade 5 and recorded that threatened punishments and the inner play's deaths are not dramatized in its selected scenes, a selection it said needs age and content review rather than a hidden rewrite. It kept facts the original leaves uncomfortable, such as a spell never shown removed and one character manipulating another, and its lessons preserve the coercion and uncertainty rather than claiming every character freely chooses the ending. The course's release checklist asks every adaptation for exact provenance, declared changes and an explicit age-appropriate treatment of harmful or dated material. A source audit of another grade adds that leaving chapters out of a short adaptation does not show that a specified cut was carried out.
against: A classroom guide in the sources wants the real language confronted as a group: "For this particular scene from Othello, it is important to confront and discuss the racial and racist language as a community of learners. Students need and deserve the chance to tackle the real thing." (`g9/sources/Cutting-a-Scene-Othello-1.1.pdf`, pdftotext lines 34-36). It also expects groups that keep the slurs to treat them seriously rather than make light of them (lines 113-115).

evidence.quote: The retelling preserves those limits and avoids presenting coercion as healthy relationship advice.

The introductory unit is not the full play. Threatened punishments and the inner play's deaths are not dramatized in the selected Grade5 scenes. This selection requires age/content review, not a hidden rewrite
Preserve the coercion and uncertainty rather than claiming every character freely chooses the ending.
Every adaptation has exact provenance and declared changes; every quote is present; potentially harmful or dated source material has an explicit age-appropriate editorial treatment.
Current short adaptations cannot be claimed to have executed those cuts merely because they omit the corresponding chapters.
